summary: Accumulate Euclidean adjacent-vertex distances from zero

capability: Accumulate Euclidean adjacent-vertex chord lengths from zero along an ordered planar polyline.
operation: ordered planar vertices -> cumulative chord-length distance
discovery.model: Exact polygonal chord lengths, not a smooth-curve arclength.
discovery.geometry: Planar ordered vertices in coherent length units; only adjacent-vertex distances are accumulated.
discovery.boundary: Distance starts at zero and no implicit closing segment is added; finite ordered planar vertices are required.

identity.direction: Declared inputs to Cumulative path distance
identity.definition: Accumulate Euclidean adjacent-vertex distances from zero
identity.coordinates: Planar pairs in coherent length units
identity.boundary: Starts at zero; no implicit closing segment

outputs.name: distance
outputs.constraints: Nondecreasing; duplicate vertices give zero increments

supported: Finite inputs satisfying the callable-specific shape, support, and boundary conditions
excluded: No true smooth-curve arclength or implicit closure

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError or the underlying NumPy/SciPy exception for nonfinite, mismatched, unsorted, out-of-domain, or malformed inputs; no input repair is inferred.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical, interpolation, or optional-dependency exceptions propagate from the direct calculation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the relation uses direct finite-difference, interpolation, selection, or quadrature operations.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is promised when input validation or the underlying numerical operation fails.

example.description: Accumulate Euclidean distance along a two-segment polyline.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry.sampling import get_fieldline_distance

points = np.array([[0.0, 0.0], [3.0, 0.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
np.testing.assert_allclose(get_fieldline_distance(points), [0.0, 3.0, 7.0])
